title: Authentication and authorization in one screen
rememberThis: Authentication = who (401 if missing/invalid). Authorization = what (403 if policy fails).
JWT is signed, not encrypted — never put secrets in payload; validate iss, aud, exp, signature.
Refresh tokens go to token endpoint only — BFF + HttpOnly cookie for browsers; access JWT to API.
Policies + IAuthorizationHandler beat scattered User.IsInRole checks; resource handlers fix BOLA.
API keys: hash at rest, header transport, per-client rate limits — not a query string.
bullets: Pipeline order: UseRouting → UseAuthentication → UseAuthorization → MapControllers.
RoleClaimType and MapInboundClaims=false (.NET 8) must match your IdP token shape.
OAuth: authorization code + PKCE for users; client credentials for services; API validates access token.
FallbackPolicy RequireAuthenticatedUser secures entire API — mark public routes [AllowAnonymous].
OWASP API #1 BOLA: AuthorizeAsync(User, entity, policy) after loading by id from route.
OnAuthenticationFailed / 403 audit logs — never log Bearer tokens or raw API keys.

rows.label: 401 vs 403
rows.value: 401 = AuthN failed or no credentials; 403 = AuthN ok, AuthZ denied

rows.label: JWT vs session
rows.value: JWT scales stateless; sessions revoke instantly — short TTL + refresh rotation

rows.label: Interview trap
rows.value: Treating JWT as encrypted; using ID token to call API; API keys in query string

rows.label: Diagnostics
rows.value: JwtBearerEvents, JWKS refresh, Application Insights 401/403 ratio, rate limit 429 metrics
